Quantitative Aptitude is part of the official GATE CSE 2027 syllabus. Study definitions, standard problems, and trace examples by hand.

1. Read key concepts and definitions

3. Review frequently asked GATE concepts
4. Solve related PYQs
5. Attempt topic-wise mock test
6. Mark revision needed for weak areas

### General Aptitude context

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the time complexity of the following recurrence? T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1)
mocktestquestions.explanation: T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1) solves to T(n) = O(n).

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of size n?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each iteration, giving O(log n) time.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Merge Sort has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Quick Sort has worst-case O(n^2) when pivot is poorly chosen (e.g., sorted array).

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: How many comparisons does heap sort require in the worst case to sort n elements?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Heap sort requires O(n log n) comparisons in the worst case.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: In Dijkstra's algorithm, which data structure gives the best asymptotic complexity?
mocktestquestions.explanation: A min-heap priority queue gives O((V+E) log V) complexity for Dijkstra.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: The Bellman-Ford algorithm can detect negative weight cycles. How many iterations of edge relaxation are needed in the worst case for a graph with V vertices?
mocktestquestions.explanation: V-1 relaxations find shortest paths; a Vth iteration detects negative cycles.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Kruskal's algorithm for MST uses which data structure to detect cycles efficiently?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Union-Find with path compression detects cycles in near-constant time per operation.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: The 0/1 Knapsack problem with n items and capacity W is solved in which time using DP?
mocktestquestions.explanation: The DP table is of size (n+1) x (W+1), giving O(nW) time.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: The Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) of two strings of lengths m and n can be found in O(mn) time. What is the space-optimized complexity?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Only the previous row is needed, so space can be reduced to O(min(m,n)).

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following problems does NOT exhibit optimal substructure?
options: Longest path in an unweighted graph
mocktestquestions.explanation: Longest path in an unweighted graph does not exhibit optimal substructure (NP-hard).

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which problem is solved optimally by a greedy approach?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Fractional Knapsack is solved greedily by taking the highest value-to-weight ratio items.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Prim's algorithm builds a Minimum Spanning Tree by:
options: Adding the cheapest edge that connects a visited vertex to an unvisited one
Sorting all edges and picking the cheapest
mocktestquestions.explanation: Prim's algorithm grows the MST by adding the cheapest edge from the current set.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: The Master Theorem solves recurrences of which form?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Master Theorem applies to T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n) where a >= 1, b > 1.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Using Master Theorem, what is the solution to T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Case 2: a=2, b=2, f(n)=n = n^log2(2), so T(n) = O(n log n).

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: The Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) algorithm preprocesses the pattern in which time?
options: O(n) where n is text length
O(m) where m is pattern length
mocktestquestions.explanation: The prefix function (LPS array) is computed in O(m) time during preprocessing.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about NP-complete problems?
options: All NP-complete problems can be solved in polynomial time
If any NP-complete problem can be solved in polynomial time, then P = NP
NP-complete problems cannot be verified in polynomial time
NP-complete problems are not in NP
mocktestquestions.explanation: If any NP-complete problem has polynomial-time solution, then all NP problems do (P = NP).

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the time complexity of accessing the ith element in an array?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Array access is O(1) since elements are stored contiguously.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: In open addressing with linear probing, the hash function is h(k, i) = (h(k) + i) mod m. What is the primary disadvantage?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Linear probing causes primary clustering where consecutive occupied slots form long runs.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: In a Binary Search Tree, what order does inorder traversal produce?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Inorder traversal of a BST visits nodes in non-decreasing order.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Minimum comparisons in worst case to find the largest element in an unsorted array of n elements?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Finding the maximum requires n-1 comparisons in the worst case.

mocktestquestions.subject: AL
mocktestquestions.questionText: Matrix chain multiplication with n matrices has optimal substructure. Minimum multiplications can be found in which time?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Matrix chain multiplication DP uses O(n^2) space and O(n^3) time.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the time complexity to access the ith element in an array?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Array elements are stored contiguously; access is O(1) using base + offset.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: A 2D array A[10][20] stored in row-major order. How many elements precede A[5][10]?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Elements before row 5: 5 * 20 = 100; in row 5 before col 10: 10; total = 110.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching for an element in a sorted array of size n?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Binary search on a sorted array takes O(log n) worst-case time.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the time complexity to insert a node at the beginning of a singly linked list?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Insertion at head requires updating the new node next pointer and the head pointer, both O(1).

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: To detect a cycle in a linked list, which algorithm is commonly used?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Floyd's algorithm uses slow and fast pointers; if they meet, a cycle exists.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Given pointers to two singly linked lists that intersect, what is the time complexity to find the intersection node?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Find lengths, advance the longer list by the difference, then traverse both together O(n+m).

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which data structure is used to implement recursion?
mocktestquestions.explanation: The call stack stores return addresses and local variables for each recursive call.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: A queue is implemented using two stacks. Enqueue pushes onto S1. Dequeue pops from S2 if non-empty, else transfers all from S1 to S2 and pops. What is the amortized time of dequeue?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Each element is moved at most once from S1 to S2, giving O(1) amortized time.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: In a complete binary tree with n nodes, what is the height?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Height of a complete binary tree = floor(log2(n)) = ceil(log2(n+1)) - 1.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h (root at height 0)?
mocktestquestions.explanation: A full binary tree of height h has 2^(h+1) - 1 nodes.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Worst-case time complexity of searching in a BST with n nodes:
mocktestquestions.explanation: In a skewed BST, search degenerates to O(n) like a linked list.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which traversal of a BST produces elements in sorted order?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Inorder traversal of a BST visits nodes in non-decreasing order.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: In a min-heap of n elements, where can the largest element be located?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Every parent is smaller than its children, so the largest must be a leaf.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Best time to build a heap from an unsorted array of n elements using build-heap (heapify):
mocktestquestions.explanation: Bottom-up heapify takes O(n) time as most nodes are near the bottom.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which collision resolution technique is most susceptible to primary clustering?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Linear probing causes primary clustering as consecutive occupied slots form long runs.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: DFS on a graph with V vertices and E edges (adjacency list) has which complexity?
mocktestquestions.explanation: DFS visits each vertex once and explores each edge once, O(V+E).

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: For BFS on a graph, which data structure is used to store the frontier?
mocktestquestions.explanation: BFS uses a queue to process vertices level by level.

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: What does the recursive function f(n) = 1 if n <= 1, else f(n-1) + f(n-2) compute?
mocktestquestions.explanation: This is the standard recursive definition of Fibonacci: Fib(0)=1, Fib(1)=1, Fib(n)=Fib(n-1)+Fib(n-2).

mocktestquestions.subject: DS
mocktestquestions.questionText: In C, what does strlen("Hello") return?
mocktestquestions.explanation: strlen counts characters until the null terminator, so "Hello" has length 5.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the role of a lexical analyzer?
mocktestquestions.explanation: The lexer reads the source code and produces a stream of tokens.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Regular expressions and finite automata are used for which phase?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Lexical analysis uses REs for token patterns and FAs for token recognition.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a typical token class?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Parse trees are produced by parsing, not by lexical analysis.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which parsing technique can parse the full class of deterministic context-free grammars?
mocktestquestions.explanation: LR(1) parsers handle all DCFGs, while LL(1) handles a proper subset.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: An LL(1) parser requires the grammar to be:
options: Non-left-recursive with disjoint FIRST sets for each production
mocktestquestions.explanation: LL(1) requires no left recursion and disjoint FIRST sets for each production.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: In shift-reduce parsing, what is a handle?
options: A substring that matches a production right-hand side
mocktestquestions.explanation: A handle is a substring matching the RHS of a production that will be reduced.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: A synthesized attribute at a node depends on:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Synthesized attributes are computed upward from children to parent.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: In an L-attributed SDD, attributes can be evaluated in:
mocktestquestions.explanation: L-attributed definitions allow evaluation in a single left-to-right traversal.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Three Address Code uses at most how many operands per instruction?
mocktestquestions.explanation: TAC has the form: result = operand1 op operand2, with at most three addresses.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: A quadruple has which fields?
mocktestquestions.explanation: A quadruple stores: operator, operand1, operand2, and result.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Loop-invariant code motion moves invariant computations to:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Loop-invariant computations are moved to the loop preheader to avoid redundant execution.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Dead code elimination removes:
options: Code whose results are never used
mocktestquestions.explanation: Dead code is code whose computed values are never used in subsequent computations.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which data structure is commonly used to implement a symbol table?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Hash tables provide O(1) average-case lookup for symbol table operations.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: In languages with nested procedures, how are non-local variables accessed?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Static chains link stack frames to access variables from statically enclosing scopes.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Panic mode error recovery skips tokens until:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Panic mode discards tokens until a token in the FOLLOW set or synchronization token is found.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: Graph coloring register allocation uses which concept?
options: Live variable analysis and interference graph
mocktestquestions.explanation: An interference graph is built where edges connect variables that cannot share a register.

mocktestquestions.subject: CD
mocktestquestions.questionText: The regex a(b|c)*a matches:
options: Strings starting and ending with a, with any bs and cs in between
Strings with only a and b
Strings with equal bs and cs
mocktestquestions.explanation: The regex matches a, followed by zero or more bs or cs, then a.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which OSI layer handles routing and forwarding?
mocktestquestions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for routing and logical addressing.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which OSI layer provides hop-to-hop error detection and correction?
mocktestquestions.explanation: The Data Link Layer handles framing, error detection, and MAC.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which protocol resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses?
mocktestquestions.explanation: ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses on a local network.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: HTTP uses which transport layer protocol?
mocktestquestions.explanation: HTTP uses TCP for reliable data transfer on port 80 (or 443 for HTTPS).

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is TRUE about TCP?
options: It provides reliable, connection-oriented service with flow and congestion control
It uses only IP for addressing
mocktestquestions.explanation: TCP provides reliable, ordered, connection-oriented data transfer.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: TCP slow start increases the congestion window:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Slow start doubles the congestion window each RTT until threshold is reached.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: What is the subnet mask for a /27 CIDR network?

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: A router receives a packet with destination 192.168.5.10. It has routes: 192.168.5.0/24 via 10.0.0.1, 192.168.0.0/16 via 10.0.0.2, 0.0.0.0/0 via 10.0.0.3. Which route is chosen?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Longest prefix match: /24 is more specific than /16 for 192.168.5.10.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: TCP three-way handshake sequence:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Client sends SYN, server responds with SYN-ACK, client sends ACK.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: UDP provides which of the following?
mocktestquestions.explanation: UDP is connectionless and provides best-effort delivery without reliability guarantees.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which protocol is used to send email?
mocktestquestions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending email.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: DNS primarily uses which transport protocol?
mocktestquestions.explanation: DNS uses UDP for queries and TCP for zone transfers and large responses.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: In CSMA/CD, after a collision, the station:
options: Waits a random time using exponential backoff
mocktestquestions.explanation: Exponential backoff ensures random wait times to reduce collision probability.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: Hamming distance between 1010101 and 1100110 is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: 1010101 XOR 1100110 = 0110011, which has 4 one bits, so distance = 4.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which is a symmetric key encryption algorithm?
mocktestquestions.explanation: DES is a symmetric block cipher. RSA and Diffie-Hellman are asymmetric.

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: In RSA, given p=7, q=11, e=17, what is the private key d?

mocktestquestions.subject: CN
mocktestquestions.questionText: IEEE 802.11 (WiFi) uses which collision avoidance mechanism?
mocktestquestions.explanation: CSMA/CA is used in wireless because collision detection is not practical.

mocktestquestions.explanation: CLA computes Gi = AiBi and Pi = Ai XOR Bi, then calculates all carries in parallel.

mocktestquestions.questionText: Which is the fastest memory?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Registers are inside the CPU with near-zero access time.

mocktestquestions.questionText: A 64 KB direct-mapped cache has 64-byte blocks. How many index bits (32-bit address)?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Blocks = 64KB / 64B = 1024 = 2^10, so index = 10 bits.

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which mapping scheme has the highest conflict misses?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Direct-mapped cache has one location per block, causing the most conflict misses.

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: A 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB). Cycles for N instructions without hazards:
mocktestquestions.explanation: First instruction: 5 cycles. Each subsequent: 1 cycle. Total = 5 + (N-1) = N + 4.

mocktestquestions.explanation: Forwarding routes ALU output directly to the dependent instruction input.

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: RISC design philosophy favors:
options: Variable-length instructions with many addressing modes
Fixed-length instructions with simple addressing modes
mocktestquestions.explanation: RISC uses fixed-length instructions and simple addressing modes for efficient pipelining.

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: Base/indexed addressing computes EA as:
mocktestquestions.explanation: EA = Base Register + Offset (or index register).

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: In DMA, who controls the data transfer between I/O and memory?
mocktestquestions.explanation: The DMA controller manages data transfer between memory and I/O devices directly.

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: Interrupt overhead is 50 cycles, device generates 1000 interrupts/s. At 1 GHz, fraction of CPU time spent on interrupts?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Cycles for interrupts = 50 * 1000 = 50000. Fraction = 50000 / 10^9 = 0.005%.

mocktestquestions.subject: CO
mocktestquestions.questionText: CPU execution time formula:
mocktestquestions.explanation: CPU Time = (CPI * Instruction Count) / Clock Rate.

mocktestquestions.questionText: Processor at 2 GHz, CPI = 1.5. Time to execute 10^9 instructions?

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: In an ER diagram, which symbol represents a relationship set?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Diamonds represent relationship sets, rectangles represent entity sets, ellipses represent attributes.

options: The primary key of another entity (owner) combined with a partial discriminator
mocktestquestions.explanation: Weak entities are identified by the owner key plus a partial discriminator.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB

options: It must be a single attribute
There can be only one candidate key per relation
mocktestquestions.explanation: A candidate key is a minimal superkey (no proper subset is a superkey).

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which SQL clause filters groups after GROUP BY?
mocktestquestions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY, WHERE filters rows before grouping.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: SQL NATURAL JOIN on R(A,B) and S(B,C) is equivalent to:
options: SELECT * FROM R, S WHERE R.B = S.B
SELECT * FROM R INNER JOIN S ON R.A = S.C
SELECT * FROM R CROSS JOIN S
SELECT * FROM R LEFT JOIN S ON R.B = S.B
mocktestquestions.explanation: NATURAL JOIN joins on all common columns (B in this case).

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which SQL keyword removes duplicate rows from results?
mocktestquestions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result set.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and:
mocktestquestions.explanation: 2NF eliminates partial dependencies where a non-prime attribute depends on part of a candidate key.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: R(A,B,C,D) with FDs {AB -> C, C -> D, D -> A}. How many candidate keys?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Candidate keys: AB (AB+ = ABCD), BC (BC+ = BCDA), BD (BD+ = BDAC). Total = 3.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial FD X -> Y:
mocktestquestions.explanation: BCNF requires that X be a superkey for every non-trivial FD X -> Y.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which is NOT an ACID property?
mocktestquestions.explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: In Two-Phase Locking (2PL), the growing phase:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Growing phase: locks acquired only. Shrinking phase: locks released only.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB

mocktestquestions.explanation: Precedence graph: T1->T2 (R1A before W2A) and T2->T1 (W2A before W1A). Cycle, not serializable.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: In a B+ tree of order p (max children), max keys per internal node:
mocktestquestions.explanation: An internal node has at most p children and at most p-1 keys.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB
mocktestquestions.questionText: B+ tree order 4 (max 4 children) has 125 keys. Minimum height (root height 0)?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Min leaf keys = ceil(4/2)-1 = 1. Height 0: 1 leaf, 1 key. Height 1: 2 children, 2 keys. Height 2: 4 children, 4 keys. Height 3: 8 children... Actually with order 4, each internal node has min ceil(4/2)=2 children. Max keys per leaf = 3. At height 3: at most 4*4*4 = 64 leaves * 3 = 192 keys. At height 2: 4*4=16 leaves * 3 = 48 keys. So minimum height = 3.

mocktestquestions.subject: DB

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: If the 5th day of a month is Tuesday, what is the 20th day?
mocktestquestions.explanation: 5th is Tuesday. 15th (5+10) is also Tuesday (10 mod 7 = 3 days after). 5+15=20: 15 days later = 15 mod 7 = 1 day after Tuesday = Wednesday.

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: In a certain code, GATE is written as HZSD. How is EXAM written?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the previous letter: G->F, A->Z, T->S, E->D gives FZSD. Similarly EXAM: E->D, X->W, A->Z, M->L gives DWZL.

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: A pie chart shows 25% for sector A. What is the central angle?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Central angle = 25% of 360 = (25/100) * 360 = 90 degrees.

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: If a:b = 2:3 and b:c = 4:5, what is a:c?

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19
mocktestquestions.explanation: All are odd numbers, but 3,7,11,19 are prime. 15 is composite.

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: A bar graph shows sales: Jan=100, Feb=150, Mar=120. Percentage increase from Jan to Feb:

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
mocktestquestions.explanation: At 3:15, minute hand at 3, hour hand moved 1/4 of the way to 4 = 7.5 degrees past 3. Angle = 7.5 degrees.

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: Choose the correct word: She ___ to the store yesterday.
mocktestquestions.explanation: The past tense of "go" is "went", which matches "yesterday".

mocktestquestions.subject: APT
mocktestquestions.questionText: Choose the antonym of "Amplify":
mocktestquestions.explanation: "Reduce" is the antonym of "Amplify" (to make larger).

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which system call creates a new process in Unix?
mocktestquestions.explanation: fork() creates a new process by duplicating the calling process.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: A process that terminates before its parent can become:
mocktestquestions.explanation: A zombie process is a terminated process whose parent has not yet called wait().

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which scheduling algorithm minimizes average waiting time?
mocktestquestions.explanation: SJF is provably optimal for minimizing average waiting time.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: In Round Robin scheduling, if time quantum is too large, it degenerates to:
mocktestquestions.explanation: A very large quantum makes Round Robin behave like FCFS (no preemption).

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: A multilevel feedback queue allows:
mocktestquestions.explanation: Multilevel feedback queue allows processes to move between queues based on their behavior.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following is a condition for deadlock?
options: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait
Only mutual exclusion and hold and wait
mocktestquestions.explanation: All four conditions (mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait) are necessary for deadlock.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which technique allows a process to be larger than physical memory?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Virtual memory allows a process to be larger than physical memory using demand paging.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: In paging, a logical address consists of:
mocktestquestions.explanation: A logical address is divided into page number (p) and page offset (d).

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Thrashing occurs when:
options: The system spends more time paging than executing
mocktestquestions.explanation: Thrashing is when the page fault rate is so high that the system spends most time paging.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Page size = 4 KB, page table entry = 4 bytes. Page table size for 32-bit address space:
mocktestquestions.explanation: 32-bit address = 4 GB. Pages = 4GB/4KB = 2^32/2^12 = 2^20 entries. Each entry 4 bytes = 2^20 * 4 = 4 MB.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: A TLB hit takes 10 ns, miss takes 100 ns (page table access). TLB hit rate = 99%. Effective memory access time:

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which disk scheduling algorithm minimizes seek time by servicing the closest request first?
mocktestquestions.explanation: SSTF selects the request with the minimum seek time from the current head position.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: In a Unix inode, which of the following is NOT a pointer type?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Inodes use direct, single indirect, double indirect, and triple indirect pointers.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which file allocation method suffers from external fragmentation?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Contiguous allocation suffers from external fragmentation similar to memory allocation.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: A semaphore initialized to 1 is known as:
mocktestquestions.explanation: A semaphore with value 1 is a binary semaphore, often used as a mutex lock.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: The Producer-Consumer problem with a bounded buffer requires:
options: Two semaphores (empty and full) plus a mutex
mocktestquestions.explanation: Bounded buffer needs semaphores for empty, full, and a mutex for buffer access.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: Banker algorithm is used for:
mocktestquestions.explanation: The Banker algorithm is a deadlock avoidance algorithm that checks safe states.

mocktestquestions.subject: OS
mocktestquestions.questionText: FCFS scheduling is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: FCFS is non-preemptive; once a process starts, it runs until completion or blocking.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which automaton recognizes regular languages?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Finite automata recognize regular languages (Type 3 in Chomsky hierarchy).

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: The language L = {a^n b^n | n >= 0} is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: a^n b^n requires counting, which a finite automaton cannot do, but a PDA can.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a regular language?
options: Set of all strings ending with 00
Set of all strings with equal number of 0s and 1s
Set of all strings containing 101 as substring
Set of all strings of length divisible by 3
mocktestquestions.explanation: Equal number of 0s and 1s requires counting, which is not possible with finite automata.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: The pumping lemma for regular languages is used to:
options: Prove that a language is NOT regular
mocktestquestions.explanation: The pumping lemma is a tool to prove that certain languages are not regular.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: L = {a^n b^m | n mod 2 = 0, m >= 0}. This language is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: This is regular because n mod 2 = 0 is a finite condition (even number of as), and b^m is arbitrary. A DFA needs only 2 states for as then accept bs.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: A Pushdown Automaton (PDA) has an additional memory element:
mocktestquestions.explanation: A PDA extends an NFA with a stack, allowing it to recognize context-free languages.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following languages is context-free?
options: ww where w is a binary string
mocktestquestions.explanation: a^n b^n is context-free (recognized by a PDA). a^n b^n c^n is context-sensitive.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: A context-free grammar G = (V, T, P, S). What does P represent?
mocktestquestions.explanation: P is the set of production rules of the form A -> alpha where A is a variable.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: The grammar S -> aSb | ab generates which language?
mocktestquestions.explanation: S derives a^n S b^n and finally ab, giving a^n b^n for n >= 1.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which automaton can recognize recursively enumerable languages?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Turing machines recognize recursively enumerable languages (Type 0).

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: The Halting Problem is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: The Halting Problem asks whether a TM halts on given input; it is undecidable.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: A language is recursively enumerable if it is accepted by:
options: A Turing Machine that halts on all inputs
A Turing Machine (may loop for non-members)
mocktestquestions.explanation: RE languages are accepted by a TM that may not halt on strings not in the language.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: PCP is undecidable; there is no algorithm to solve all instances of PCP.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Which of the following is decidable?
mocktestquestions.explanation: Membership (whether a string is generated by a CFG) is decidable (CYK algorithm). Others for CFGs are undecidable.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: L = {w in {0,1}* | w contains 101 as substring}. This is:
mocktestquestions.explanation: The set of all strings containing a substring can be recognized by a DFA, so it is regular.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: A CFG is ambiguous if:
options: It has more than one leftmost derivation for some string
mocktestquestions.explanation: Ambiguity means there exists at least one string with multiple leftmost (or rightmost) derivations.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: Church-Turing thesis states that:
options: Every effectively computable function can be computed by a Turing machine
TMs are more powerful than computers
mocktestquestions.explanation: The Church-Turing thesis states that any effectively computable function can be computed by a Turing machine.

mocktestquestions.subject: TOC
mocktestquestions.questionText: The minimum number of states in a DFA accepting strings ending with 00 over {0,1}:
mocktestquestions.explanation: A DFA with 3 states is needed: initial, after one 0, and after two consecutive 0s (accepting).

dailycontents.subject: Computer Networks
dailycontents.title: TCP Congestion Control
dailycontents.content: TCP uses slow start (exponential window growth), congestion avoidance (linear growth), fast retransmit (3 duplicate ACKs), and fast recovery. AIMD ensures fair bandwidth sharing across flows.

dailycontents.subject: DBMS
dailycontents.title: Join Query
dailycontents.content: Write SQL to find employees who earn more than their department average salary using a correlated subquery or window function.
dailycontents.explanation: SELECT e.name FROM emp e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp WHERE dept_id = e.dept_id)

dailycontents.subject: Computer Organization
dailycontents.title: Average Memory Access Time
dailycontents.content: AMAT = Hit Time + Miss Rate × Miss Penalty
dailycontents.explanation: Fundamental formula for cache performance analysis questions.

dailycontents.subject: Algorithms
dailycontents.title: GATE 2021 – 0/1 Knapsack
dailycontents.content: Given items with weights and values, find maximum value that fits in knapsack of capacity W using DP.
dailycontents.explanation: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w-wt[i]] + val[i]). Space can be optimized to O(W).

dailycontents.subject: TOC
dailycontents.title: Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages
dailycontents.content: If L is regular, there exists pumping length p such that any string s in L with |s| ≥ p can be written as s=xyz where |xy|≤p, |y|≥1, and xyⁱz ∈ L for all i≥0. Used to prove languages are NOT regular.

dailycontents.subject: Operating Systems
dailycontents.title: Banker's Algorithm
dailycontents.content: Consider a system with 3 processes and 3 resource types. Given Available = (3,3,2), Allocation matrix, and Max matrix – determine if the system is in a safe state.
dailycontents.explanation: Apply Banker's algorithm: find a safe sequence where each process can finish with currently available resources.

dailycontents.subject: Algorithms
dailycontents.title: Master Theorem
dailycontents.content: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n) → compare f(n) with n^(log_b a) to determine Θ bound
dailycontents.explanation: Used to solve recurrence relations for divide-and-conquer algorithms.

dailycontents.subject: Operating Systems
dailycontents.title: GATE 2022 – Deadlock Detection
dailycontents.content: Given a resource allocation graph, determine if the system has deadlock and identify processes in the deadlock cycle.
dailycontents.explanation: Build wait-for graph from allocation/request matrices. Cycle in wait-for graph indicates deadlock.
